anchors.paper_title: Acquisition and processing of Motor Imagery and Motor Execution Dataset (MIMED) for six movement activities
anchors.reason: The Data in Brief paper by Wirawan et al. 2024 describes the MIMED dataset (Emotiv EPOC X, 14 channels, 30 participants, motor imagery), matching this dataset's DOI, authors and acquisition.
The DANS/Mendeley 'MIMED' record is the original deposit of the same data: Wirawan et al., Emotiv EPOC X 14 channels, 30 Bali students, two days, motor imagery and execution.

anchors.paper_title: MNE-BIDS: Organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format and facilitating their analysis
anchors.paper_venue: The Journal of Open Source Software
anchors.reason: MNE-BIDS is a software tool for organizing electrophysiology data into BIDS, used for dataset conversion, not a paper describing the MIMED2024 motor imagery dataset.

anchors.paper_title: EEG-BIDS, an extension to the brain imaging data structure for electroencephalography
anchors.reason: EEG-BIDS is a specification/extension of BIDS for EEG data organization, a standard used by this dataset, not the MIMED2024 data paper (Wirawan et al., Data in Brief).

metadata.methods_description: EEG was recorded with a 14-channel Emotiv EPOC X headset (saline felt sensors, 128 Hz, standard 10-20 montage, CMS/DRL reference) from 30 subjects across 2 sessions of 6 runs each. Participants imagined movements cued by video, with trials spanning 0-4 s. Original EDF files were converted to MAT and then to BIDS using MOABB.

citation_details.title: A multi-paradigm EEG dataset for studying upper limb rehabilitation exercises
citation_details.author: Wenwen Chang, Weixuan Kong, Guanghui Yan, Renjie Lv, Kaiyue Du, Muhammad Tariq Sadiq, Bin Guo, Rong Yin, Xuan Liu
citation_details.abstract: Most stroke survivors experience persistent upper limb motor dysfunction, and brain-computer interface (BCI) rehabilitation technologies have been widely explored to address this issue. However, systematic comparisons and analyses of differences among rehabilitation paradigms remain challenging due to the lack of multi-paradigm EEG datasets from the same subjects. This study aims to construct an EEG dataset that collects various rehabilitation paradigms for the same subjects. A total of 28 healthy subjects were recruited, and EEG data were collected under six types of upper limb rehabilitation paradigms. Each paradigm involves two or three actions, including grasping and releasing with the left, right, or both hands. The dataset includes both raw EEG signals and preprocessed versions with bandpass filtering and artifact removal. citation_details.title: Hybrid method for optimizing emotion recognition models on electroencephalogram signals
citation_details.author: I. Wirawan, Kadek Yota Ernanda Aryanto, I. N. Sukajaya, Ni Nyoman Mestri Agustini, Dewi Arum Widhiyanti Metra Putri
citation_details.venue: IAES International Journal of Artificial Intelligence (IJ-AI)
citation_details.abstract: Two critical factors that need to be studied in emotion recognition are the differences in electroencephalogram (EEG) signal patterns caused by participant characteristics and EEG signals with spatial information. These factors significantly affect the resulting accuracy. The model proposed in this study can consider these factors. This model consists of the modified weighted mean filter method for the basic EEG signal smoothing process, the differential entropy method for the feature extraction process, the relative difference method for the baseline reduction, the 3D cube method for feature representation, and the continuous capsule network method for the classification process. Based on testing on three public datasets, this hybrid method can overcome factors affecting emotion recognition accuracy. This statement is based on the accuracy produced by this model, which outperformed the accuracy validated in previous studies.

citation_details.title: EEG Motor Execution Classification Using RG-CNN-LSTM: A Riemannian Geometry-Inspired Deep Learning Approach
citation_details.author: Md. Jewel Rana, Nakib Aman, Avi Roy, S. M. Mehdi Hasan Zim
citation_details.venue: 2025 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
citation_details.abstract: Detecting motor-related brain activity is essential for advancements in brain-computer interface (BCI) applications, particularly in neurorehabilitation and assistive technologies. While traditional methods have identified certain characteristics of motor-related electroencephalograms (EEGs), this study proposes a novel approach leveraging Riemannian geometry (RG)-based features and hybrid deep learning architectures. In particular, a hybrid RG-CNN-LSTM model was developed and evaluated, achieving the highest classification accuracy of 82.28% under a five-fold cross-validation scheme. In addition, we compared five machine learning classifiers and three deep learning models to validate the performance of our method. The proposed lightweight framework demonstrates strong potential for real-time implementation, offering effective assistance to individuals with motor impairments. citation_details.title: SSTMNet: Spectral-Spatio-Temporal and Multiscale Deep Network for EEG-Based Motor Imagery Classification
citation_details.author: Albandari Talq Alotaibi, Muhammad Hussain, Hatim Aboalsamh
citation_details.abstract: Motor impairment is a critical health issue that restricts disabled people from living their lives normally and with comfort. Detecting motor imagery (MI) in electroencephalography (EEG) signals can make their lives easier. There has been a lot of work on detecting two or four different MI movements, which include bilateral, contralateral, and unilateral upper limb movements. However, there is little research on the challenging problem of detecting more than four motor imagery tasks and unilateral lower limb movements. As a solution to this problem, a spectral-spatio-temporal multiscale network (SSTMNet) has been introduced to detect six imagery tasks. It first performs a spectral analysis of an EEG trial and attends to the salient brain waves (rhythms) using an attention mechanism.
